Notice: I’m So Sorry! Monday Releases Will Always Be Irregular!!!

Hello, this is the author!

 

Lately, I’ve had to post more notices—whether it’s because of corona or sudden health issues—and here I am writing another one.

This time, it’s about Monday releases, or more precisely, the chapters I write on Sundays and post at 12:05 AM on Mondays.

My father runs his own business, so my family always has a mandatory Sunday meal together, along with family events.

Because of that, whenever my releases are delayed, it’s always the Monday chapter that ends up late.

 

Now that I’m finally making some money, I can’t exactly become some unfilial son who skips the one weekly meal with my dad just to write.

So, I expect Monday releases will continue to be late, which is why I’m writing this notice.

 

This is due to my personal circumstances, so I hope you, the readers, will understand. I’m always sorry and grateful.

So, I’ll shout “I hate Mondays!” and take my leave.

Thank you again, and I love you all, readers.

 

 

Oh, and in my last late notice, I mentioned it was an impromptu family event, but normally, we have lunch together and spend time until dinner.

Today, though, we’re meeting now to have dinner together, which is why I’m writing this notice.

I only found out about this today while waiting for my dad at lunchtime.

 

It’s so last-minute!

Chapter 1: The Tutorial Begins 01

 

Ever heard of a retard who got turned into a corpse? A retard who lost his life getting worked up over a damn game.

 

A self-deprecating chuckle escapes my lips as I mutter to myself, drawing curious glances. Of course, a perfectly normal-looking man muttering to himself would attract attention. But since everyone around me was busy chugging their drinks, the stares only lingered briefly—no one tried to snatch my drink or stop me.

 

Even as the eyes piled on, my alcohol-soaked brain was too scrambled to stop me from cheerfully muttering to myself.

 

Lee Ha-neul, age 25. Died of a heart attack right after posting a long, profanity-laced rant on the community forums because a new male character was added to a mobile game. Not even the greatest master of prose could craft a more absurd sentence than that.

 

The start of my obsession wasn’t anything special. It was autumn, I was 22, and on the day of my military discharge, I found out a new mobile game had just launched. More fate than coincidence, I suppose. With my buzz cut still fresh, I downloaded it without hesitation.

 

The game was called *Heroines’ Chronicle*—a mobile gacha RPG that was clearly made for weebs. Eighty percent of the characters were female, and the few male characters that existed were mostly 3★ or lower, just there as fodder.

 

A turn-based RPG where you built a party of hot girls, collected their skimpy skins, and ogled at them. Even with a face thicker than a brick wall, no one in their right mind would call it a masterpiece. The game was riddled with bugs, servers crashed constantly, ranking calculations were wrong, events got canceled—

 

But there was one thing everyone agreed on: this wasn’t a masterpiece—it was a *work of art*.

 

Since it was targeting otaku, they’d poured everything into the illustrations and character models. At this point, users didn’t even get mad when the servers crashed—they just waited for the compensation: special illustrations and apology skins.

 

It was pretty fucked up that you could fill out both your main and sub parties just with apology skins, but hey, who was I to complain? If the servers crashed in winter, they’d hand out Santa Girl skins. If it happened in summer, bikini skins.

 

The real problem was the balance team—if they even *had* one. Judging by their work, the company might not have a balance team at all.

 

New limited-time pickup event! New character stronger than Bunny Girl, stronger than Nurse Outfit, stronger than Santa Girl, stronger than Cowgirl, stronger than Bikini—

 

The devs must’ve had hearts as big as their guts, because every new character came out with stats so bloated they looked like they’d been force-fed. Some people said it was fine because the tits got bigger too, but that was a minority opinion.

 

*"Save my Erika, you fucking bastards!"*

*"Raised her with love, buried her with her stats."*

*"I spent all my currency, and the next day a better version drops—what the hell?"*

*"Same Native 5-Star, but the stats differ by a whole fucking star—how is that normal?"*

 

If there were hot female characters, there were bound to be over-invested weebs. Who the hell would be happy when a perfect upgrade to their favorite character came out and flipped the leaderboards upside down? Of course, I wasn’t one of them.

 

I wasn’t the type to obsess over a single character. I was a collector-type whale who spent money to gather all the meta units.

 

If Serika came out stronger than Erika, I’d pull for both. If the main tank meta shifted, I’d pull for the new one too. People say a drizzle soaks you before you notice, but I wasn’t just standing in the rain—I was diving headfirst into the river with my wallet.

 

I blew my entire paycheck, cut back on my foodie travels, and spent my clothing budget on gacha pulls. My hobby was mobile games, and my specialty was posting deck optimizations for new characters—earning me the title of "top-tier black sheep" from the haters.

 

Ahh, it had been a damn good life.

 

At least, until the final patch.

 

In Heroines' Chronicle, characters were ranked by the number of stars they had. The minimum was Native 1-Star, and the minimum for Native 5-Star was, well, five. Even though every character could eventually be promoted to 6-Star max level, the stat differences based on their native rarity were impossible to overcome. And even among Native 5-Stars, newer characters had better stats, so the broken balance was something no one could defend.

 

[EVENT! Six Brilliant Stars Shining Bright!]

 

The problematic patch was a new character release event. A new character that started as Native 6-Star and could even go up to 7-Star? What the hell were the existing characters supposed to do now?

 

From the die-hard fans calling themselves "XX-moms" to strategy site users like me, desperate to clutch at the fragments of the shattered balance, everyone was foaming at the mouth in outrage. Typing with one hand while checking my wallet’s remaining ammo with the other.

 

No matter how much we cursed, the new character was coming out anyway—because it’d be fucking overpowered. Everyone must’ve been thinking the same thing. That’s why these bastards kept pulling this shit.

 

Right after the patch, regret set in, but hesitation didn’t. My hand moved to the payment screen. I already had my usual strategy site open as I pressed down hard on my smartphone.

 

A few taps, and 10,000 won, 100,000 won, 200,000, 300,000—fuck, you sons of bitches—

 

Maybe I was just unlucky, or maybe Native 6-Stars had a lower drop rate than Native 5-Stars, but it wasn’t until I’d blown 850,000 won that I finally saw the shimmering, rainbow-colored star. Silver for 4-Star and below, gold for 5-Star, and now rainbow for 6-Star?

 

No, but the forums had set the expected cost at 1,000,000 won, so I’d actually saved 150,000. This was a game where even the Gacha Pity System had been removed along with the developers’ mothers.

 

Lightning flashed, and a star descended from the sky, wrapping around the character’s blurred silhouette. High-quality animation reminiscent of a magical girl’s transformation scene. Brilliant golden hair, snow-white skin, clear and radiant blue eyes, a sweet voice flowing through the speakers.

 

The balance-breaking Native 6-Star pickup character had finally graced my account.

 

With just one tiny problem.

 

"Why… is it a guy…?"

 

 

※

 

 

These bastards, who tried to sell nipple-sticker reverse-bunny-girl skins as a replacement after getting censored for their "apology" summer bikini skins. Where the hell did they get the idea to shove gender equality down our throats? While pondering that, I wrote a 5,700-character "100 daily thanks" macro post every day until I died of a heart attack.

 

Then I opened my eyes and found myself in the world of Heroines' Chronicle.

 

More accurately, a jumbled world where Heroines' Chronicle’s setting had seeped into reality. Familiar RPG game elements were subtly woven into this continent.

 

But whatever, that wasn’t the important part.

 

Brilliant golden hair, snow-white skin, eyes as clear and radiant as a lake, broad shoulders, a sculpted physique—and instead of big tits, a dangling thick cock. Honestly, the body itself was perfect. With this physique, I was confident I could survive anywhere.

 

His muscular body was so powerful that it was hard to gauge just how much his stats reflected reality. With gauntlets on, he could grip hard enough to leave fingerprints in stone—though he had no idea how many kgf of grip strength that was. And in his default skin—armor, helmet, a massive shield, and a mace—he could sprint at speeds comparable to a carriage without ever tiring, as if it were nothing more than a tracksuit.

 

If he’d had a body like this back in the modern world, his life would have been so much easier.

 

With his tall, model-worthy looks, he could have coasted through life in fashion or broadcasting. A sturdy, healthy, *and* handsome muscular physique—even as a regular person, he would’ve had fan clubs. Life would’ve been a breeze.

 

Of course, that didn’t mean his looks were useless in this fantasy world.

 

Back when he had nothing but his body to his name, the waitresses at the inn would slip him extra meat in his soup just for his face. And when he was lost and clueless, the senior female adventurers had helped him out more times than he could count. Over ten years, he’d lost track of how many times his appearance had saved his ass.

 

Yeah, ten years.

 

Ten years in this godforsaken fantasy world, crawling through the dirt with a sturdy body and a pathetic mind. A decade long enough to turn a scrawny office worker—who couldn’t even wring a chicken’s neck—into a veteran warrior who could cave in an orc’s skull with a mace like it was nothing.

 

— People find a way to survive, somehow.

 

He couldn’t deny that his insane looks and stat-boosted, talent-overflowing body had kept him alive. But mentally? He’d suffered like hell to adapt. Now, a bone jutting out of a broken limb was so commonplace he couldn’t even joke about it anymore.

 

Still, he didn’t plan to spend his whole life on battlefields. Once he was famous enough as an adventurer, he’d rake in the gold, make a fortune, and then—just like every adventurer dreamed—retire to some peaceful place to run a farm or an inn.

 

At least, that’s what he thought… until *she* appeared in front of him.

 

“Wow, look at that tower! I was a little worried since it’s first-gen, but they actually pulled this off? Are they torturing an alien or something?”

 

A woman in clean, elegant celestial armor. Her flawless white skin and well-kept long hair stood out sharply against the grimy, sweat-stained medieval peasants around her.

 

“Whoa, there are so many NPCs… Oh! I’m not supposed to say that word. Ahem, I’ll get into character for the roleplay!”

 

And then there was the transparent camera drone circling her head—she was a streamer.

 

“Ahem, this must be the famed Sky Tower, the city of adventurers!”

 

Ten years since he’d fallen into this hopeless fantasy world.

 

[Join a party with streamer ‘Han Se-ah’ 0/1]

 

His first quest had begun.
